# How to Build a Quiz in Google Forms with Gemini: Step-by-Step

> **In short:** Open Google Forms in a desktop browser, click the **"Help me create"** button at the top of a blank form, and type a short brief — Gemini will draft the quiz questions for you. You'll then turn on quiz mode in Settings, review every answer, and share the link.

It's Sunday evening, you promised a quiz for tomorrow's class, and the textbook chapter is 40 pages long. Or you're a trainer with a workshop next week and you need a quick knowledge check on safety procedures. Making a quiz from scratch — finding the right questions, setting the correct answer, choosing the right format — usually takes 20 to 30 minutes of fiddling about.

Google's **Gemini** AI (the same general-purpose assistant behind many of Google's tools) is now built into Google Forms. There's a **"Help me create"** button at the top of a blank form. You describe the quiz you want in a sentence, and Gemini drafts questions and answer choices for you. Here's how to do it — and what to watch out for.

## What you need before you start

- A **personal Google account** or a **Google Workspace** account through your school or employer. Either works.
- A **desktop browser** (Chrome, Edge, Firefox, or Safari). The "Help me create" button is not available in the mobile Forms app.
- A few minutes. The draft appears in under a minute, but you'll want another 5-10 minutes to review the questions.
- The feature is rolling out gradually through 2026. If you don't see the button after the steps below, give it a few days or check that your browser is up to date.

## Step 1 — Open a new form in Google Forms

Go to **forms.google.com** in your browser and click the big **"+"** card labeled **"Blank"** to start a new form. A new, untitled form opens with one empty question already added.

You'll see a purple header bar at the top with the form title (something like "Untitled form"), a description field below it, and a single blank question. On the right side of the screen, you'll see a small **"Help me create"** button with a sparkle icon — this is the Gemini-powered panel.

💬 **Example:** Open **forms.google.com** → click **"Blank"** → look for the **"Help me create"** button at the top right.

You'll know it worked when the blank form loads and you can see the **"Help me create"** button in the top right of the page.

## Step 2 — Write a clear brief in the "Help me create" panel

Click the **"Help me create"** button. A side panel slides in from the right with a text box and a prompt that says something like *"Help me create a form"*. Click into the box and type a short description of the quiz you want.

Be specific. The more detail you give, the closer the draft will be to what you actually need. A good brief usually includes: the **topic**, the **audience** (year level, training group, etc.), the **number of questions**, the **question type** you prefer, and the **difficulty**.

💬 **Example prompt:**
*"Create an 8-question multiple-choice quiz on the water cycle for Year 4 students. Cover evaporation, condensation, precipitation, and collection. Mix 5 easy and 3 harder questions. Mark the correct answer for each one."*

You'll know it worked when you see a "Creating" or loading message in the panel, and within about 30-60 seconds the draft questions appear in your form on the left.

## Step 3 — Review and edit every question

Don't skip this. Gemini **occasionally marks a wrong answer as correct** — a common AI quirk called a **hallucination** (when an AI confidently states something that isn't true). Treat the draft as a starting point, not a finished quiz.

For each question, click into it and read it carefully. Check the question text, the answer choices, and the marked correct answer. Use the **dropdown menu at the bottom-right of each question** to change the question type if you want — for example, switch a multiple-choice question to **short answer** or **checkboxes** (where more than one answer can be correct). To delete a question you don't want, click the trash-can icon in the bottom-right corner.

💬 **Example:** Click any question → look at the dropdown at the bottom-right showing **"Multiple choice"** → click it to switch to **"Short answer"** if you prefer an open response.

You'll know it worked when every question has the wording you want, the correct answer is genuinely correct, and the question type fits what you're testing.

## Step 4 — Turn on quiz mode in Settings

To unlock automatic marking and the correct-answer fields, you need to turn the form into a quiz. Click the **Settings** tab — it's the **cog (gear) icon** at the top of the form, next to **Responses**.

In the Settings panel that opens, scroll down to the **Quizzes** section and click the toggle next to **"Make this a quiz"**. Once it's on, each question will show a small **"Answer key"** link at the bottom — click it to confirm or change which answer is marked correct, and to assign **point values** (the default is 0; set it to 1 or more per question).

💬 **Example:** Click the **cog icon** at the top → find **"Make this a quiz"** → toggle it on → click **"Answer key"** under any question to set the point value.

You'll know it worked when you see a confirmation like *"Quiz mode is on"* and each question now has an **"Answer key"** link at the bottom.

## Step 5 — Add finishing touches and preview

Before you share, take two minutes to polish. Give the form a clear title at the top (something like *"Year 4 Science: The Water Cycle — Quiz"*) and a short description telling students what the quiz covers and how long it should take.

For each question, decide whether it should be **required** (the student has to answer it to submit) — toggle this with the **"Required"** switch at the bottom-right of each question. To reorder questions, click and drag the **six-dot handle** on the right side of any question.

When you're happy, click the **eye icon** (top-right, labeled **"Preview"**) to take the quiz yourself. Answer the questions the way a student would, submit, and check that the correct answers are marked as correct.

💬 **Example:** Click the **eye icon** (top-right) → answer the questions → click **"Submit"** → confirm the right answers scored points.

You'll know it worked when the preview shows your quiz exactly as a student will see it, and submitted answers are scored correctly.

## Step 6 — Share the quiz with your students or team

Click the **"Send"** button at the top-right of the form. A pop-up gives you three sharing options: a **link** (you can also tick the box to **shorten the URL**), an **email** (enter addresses and a short message), or an **embedded snippet** for a website or learning platform.

If you teach in a school using **Google Classroom**, click the three-dot menu next to **Send** and choose **"Send via Classroom"** to push the quiz directly to a class. The form will appear as an assignment, and responses are collected automatically.

💬 **Example:** Click **"Send"** → tick **"Shorten URL"** → copy the link → paste it into your class chat or assignment.

You'll know it worked when the link opens the quiz in a browser, and (if you chose email or Classroom) the recipients receive a notification with a working link.

## Common mistakes

- **Skipping the review step.** Gemini sometimes marks a wrong answer as correct, and it occasionally invents plausible-sounding but inaccurate options. Always click every question and confirm the answer key.
- **Being too vague in the prompt.** Asking for *"a quiz on science"* produces generic questions. Asking for *"a 6-question quiz on photosynthesis for Year 7, with 4 multiple-choice and 2 short-answer questions"* produces something you can actually use.
- **Looking for "Help me create" on a phone.** The feature only works in the desktop browser version of Google Forms. Open **forms.google.com** in Chrome, Edge, Firefox, or Safari on a laptop or desktop.
- **Forgetting to turn on quiz mode.** Without toggling **"Make this a quiz"** in Settings, the form won't score answers and students won't see which questions they got right or wrong.
- **Expecting it to read uploaded files.** Gemini can't pull questions from a Google Doc, PDF, or Slide you attach. If you want questions drawn from specific material, **paste the relevant text directly into the prompt box**.

## What this means for you

- **If you're a teacher or trainer:** This can cut your quiz-making time in half for general-knowledge topics. The trick is to write a clear brief and treat the draft as a starting point — your judgement is still what makes the quiz good. For curriculum-specific questions, paste the source text into the prompt.
- **If you run a small business or community group:** Use it for quick knowledge checks — workplace safety refreshers, onboarding quizzes, volunteer training. You don't need to be a quiz expert; describe the topic and let Gemini handle the structure.
- **If you're a student or self-learner:** Paste your revision notes into the prompt and ask Gemini to quiz you on them. It's a surprisingly effective study tool, and you can regenerate fresh questions any time.
